scene:
**INT. SRINU'S APARTMENT - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT**

The wall clock shows 11:20 PM. 

SWAPNA (30) sits at the dining table, peeling garlic into a steel bowl. Calm. Her phone rests beside her.

The main door latch turns slowly. A tiny click. 

SRINU (32) slips inside, holding his shoes in his hand. He freezes when he spots Swapna. He immediately puts the shoes down, straightens his posture, and acts exhausted.

SRINU
Inka padukoledha? Nenu cheppa ga call chesi... wait cheyodhu ani.

SWAPNA
(without looking up)
Nuvvu call cheyaledhu Srinu. Six thirty ki 'bayalderuthunna' ani text pettav.

SRINU
Arre, pettana? Mind motham block aypoyi undi Swapna. Asalu em roju ra babu idi. Manager gadu sudden ga oka critical escalation pettadu. Motham team ni hold chesadu. Nenu okkadine undi solve cheyalsi vachindi.

SWAPNA
(looks up)
Acha. Mari 8:30 ki mee friend Naveen call chesi 'Srinu inka intiki raaledha, vaditho konchem pani unde' ani enduku adigadu?

Srinu pauses, eyes darting slightly.

SRINU
Ah? Naveen gaada? Ha... vadu... vadiki thelidhu. Escalation confidential. Direct client call. Top management okkallane pilicharu. Anduke Naveen ki cheppaledhu.

SWAPNA
Naveen mee project lead kada?

SRINU
Project lead ee, kaani ee issue backend architecture meeda. Vadi tech stack veru. Naku direct US onshore nunchi VP ping chesadu. Matter telikunda vadu ala phone chesesthadu prathidaniki.

SWAPNA
Sare. Mari nee phone nine-thirty nunchi switch off enduku vachindi?

SRINU
(sighs, rubbing his forehead)
Adhe pedda daridram. Conference room lo charger pettadam marchipoya. Battery dead aypoyindi. Serioustha lo charging pettadam gurthuntadha cheppu?

SWAPNA
Mari office landline enduku ring ayyi disconnect ayyindi? Nenu 10 o'clock ki reception ki chesa. Security pick chesi 'Building lo evaru leramma, ten minutes back ee lock chesam' annadu.

Srinu blinks. He clears his throat, shifting his weight.

SRINU
Ha! Exactly! Vaallu building lock chesthunnaru kabbate memu bayataki vachesam. Meeting inka aipoledhu. Client emo line lo unnadu. Em chestham? Urgent ga car lo kurchuni call continue chesam. 

SWAPNA
Car lo na?

SRINU
Avunu, road meedha nilabadi client tho matladalemu ga?

SWAPNA
Srinu... car poddunna nunchi kinda parking lo ne undi. Battery down ani auto lo vellav ga?

Srinu stares at her for two solid seconds. He doesn't miss a beat.

SRINU
Mana car ani cheppana nenu? Mana car kaadhu! Cab. Uber book cheskuni... cab lo kurchuni matladam.

SWAPNA
Uber lo kurchuni VP tho meeting matladava?

SRINU
Option leka! Kani aa driver gadu asalu manishi kaadhu Swapna. Athaniki sudden ga chest pain vachindi. Nenemo call lo unna, chusthe vadu steering meeda padipoyadu. Nuvvu cheppu, client mukhyama, manishi pranam mukhyama? 

Swapna stops peeling garlic. She looks at him steadily.

SWAPNA
Chest pain ah?

SRINU
(voice rising with defensive emotion)
Yes! Nen ventane phone cut chesesi, vadini pakkaki jaripi, nene drive cheskuntu Yashoda Hospital emergency ki theskella. Motham tension. Asalu doctor lu stretchers tho ochi... naku em ardham kaale. Valla family vallu vachevaraku nene akkada unna. Manushulanna tharvatha konchem humanity undali ga? Nuvve cheppu, nenu chesindi thappa?

SWAPNA
Kadu. Chala goppa pani.

SRINU
(relieved, loosening his collar)
Adhe kada... situation ala aypoyindi. Edho nenu thirigi vachinattu chusthav enduku?

SWAPNA
Mari Yashoda Hospital emergency lo popcorn ammuthaara?

Srinu freezes.

SRINU
Enti?

Swapna points her chin toward his chest.

SWAPNA
Nee shirt pocket lo nunchi PVR Caramel Popcorn bill bayataki kanipisthundi. Inka chethiki aa cinema band kuda theeyaledhu nuvvu.

Srinu slowly looks down. 

A bright yellow paper slip is sticking out of his pocket. On his left wrist, a neon green movie band glows under the tube light.

He stares at his wrist for a long moment, his mouth opening and closing.

SRINU
Idi... hospital lo vallu... admission band veyyadaniki try chesthe... vaddu ani cheppi...

Swapna just stares at him, waiting.

SRINU
(muttering)
Interval lo thinnanu kani asalu taste baledu Swapna. Waste cinema.
beat_summary: Srinu sneaks into the apartment late at night and attempts to act exhausted to avoid suspicion.
Swapna catches him immediately by pointing out he never called and only sent a text hours earlier.
Srinu invents a sudden office escalation to explain his lateness.
Swapna counters that his project lead Naveen called looking for him at 8:30 PM, forcing Srinu to claim it was a confidential direct client call.
Swapna questions why his phone was switched off from 9:30 PM, and Srinu claims his battery died in the conference room.
Swapna mentions the building security confirmed the office was locked at 10:00 PM, leading Srinu to claim they moved the meeting to a car.
Swapna reminds him the car has a dead battery and he took an auto, causing Srinu to pivot and claim it was an Uber cab.
When Swapna questions taking a VP meeting in an Uber, Srinu escalates the lie by claiming the driver had a chest pain emergency.
Srinu describes driving the cab to Yashoda Hospital and staying to help, playing the card of pure humanity.
Swapna completely shatters the elaborate rescue story by pointing out the PVR caramel popcorn bill and cinema wristband on him.
Srinu tries one final, absurd recovery claiming the hospital tried to put an admission band on him, before weakly criticizing the movie flavor.

scene:
**EXT. AMBERPET GHMC PLAYGROUND - DAY**

Sun beats down on hard, dry red soil. A faded coir mat is nailed onto the pitch with iron pegs. 

A handwritten slate hangs on an iron fence: *R.R. XI: 72/4 (9.1 Ovs) - NEED 14 RUNS IN 11 BALLS.*

ANJI (26) stands at the crease. Full white cricket trousers, branded sweatband on his left wrist, grip tape wound neatly around his bat handle. He looks every bit like a district player, except his eyes are darting nervously.

At the non-striker end, BABU (25) leans on his bat, wearing faded track pants and hawai chappals. He spits into the dirt.

SURESH (30), the mutual-friend leg umpire, sits on an upside-down plastic crate sipping chai from a small glass.

At the bowling mark, JAVEED (24)—tall, lanky, sleeves rolled up, grinning—polishes a scuffed tennis ball against his thigh.

Javeed bowls. Medium pace, skidding off the mat. 

Anji attempts an elaborate, cover drive, lifting his elbow high. 

*THWACK.* 

He mistimes it completely. The ball trickles straight to short extra cover. Dot ball.

A couple of colony boys on the boundary snicker. 

Anji freezes in his follow-through for two full seconds, holding the pose. Then he slowly lowers the bat, glaring at the surface with deep theatrical suspicion.

ANJI
(shaking his head, clicking tongue)
Chi chi... adhe anukunna.

BABU
Rey Anji! Ball thagalaledha? Run leka sachava?

Anji ignores Babu. He walks straight to Suresh, holding the ball out between two fingers like it’s contaminated.

ANJI
Suresh anna, ball chusava idi?

SURESH
(tea cup in hand)
Emindi ra, round gaane undi ga?

ANJI
Round ga unte saripodha anna? Inside weight poyindi. Pithukku aypoyindi motham. Sponge laaga compress avthundi. Look at the seam. 

Javeed strolls up, hands on his hips.

JAVEED
Em Anji bhai, swing aytalledha?

ANJI
Swing gurinchi nuvvu naku cheppalsina avasaram ledhu Javeed. Ball lo pressure lekapothe bat middle tagilina travel avvadhu. Nenu proper timing tho punch chesa. Minimum boundary vellali. Ball flat aypoyi akkade aagipoyindi. This is not standard. Change cheyali.

Javeed’s eyes light up with pure malice. He reaches into his kit bag lying near the umpire.

JAVEED
Ball marchala? Sare. Brand new red Nivia Heavy tennis ball undi. Just last match lo rendu balls e vesam. Inka shine kuda pole. Idi okay na?

The ball Javeed pulls out is dark red, rock-hard, with zero fur left on it. A lethal missile on a concrete-backed mat.

Anji’s throat goes dry. His eyes widen for a split-second.

Babu immediately drops his bat and rushes down the pitch, panic all over his face.

BABU
(whispering furiously)
Rey! Rey bewakoof! Vadi chethiki kotha Nivia ball isthunnava ra?!

ANJI
(stiff, keeping his voice low)
Babu, technical ga standard ball unte—

BABU
Nee yamma technical! Paatha ball metthaga undi kabatte vadu bouncers veyyalekapoyadu! Aa ball tho aaram ga thirigi thirigi single lu theesi match gelichedhi unde ra! Kotha ball theesthe vadu direct gunde meedhaki visurthadu!

ANJI
(puffing his chest out)
Nuvvu aaguthava konchem? Proper cricket aadali eppudaina. Heavy ball aithe bat flow clean ga untadi. Pace manaki advantage. Nuvvu non-striker lo undi just watch the timing.

Babu stares at him like he wants to murder him on the pitch.

BABU
Manaki entry fee rendu vandhalu padindi Anji. Nenu bat break ayna parledhu kani gelavali.

ANJI
(turning to Javeed, casual)
Ha, Javeed. Pettu adhi. At least cricket aadinattu untadi.

Javeed grins, walking back. He marks a long run-up. Much longer than before.

Suresh sighs, tossing his empty tea cup into the bush.

SURESH
Ready ah? Eleven balls, fourteen runs. Play.

Anji taps his bat. Tap. Tap. He looks at Javeed sprinting in. 

Javeed hits the crease hard and hurls the new ball down the pitch with everything he’s got.

*CLACK!*

The hard ball bites the mat, kicks up viciously, and flies straight at Anji’s throat.

Anji doesn’t play a shot. He squeals, drops his bat, and literally falls flat on his back into the red dust to save his face.

The ball thuds past Suresh into the boundary wall.

SURESH
Dot ball!

Anji lies on the ground for a beat, staring at the sky. 

Babu at the other end slowly buries his face in his hands.

Anji scrambles up, dusting his knees, his white trousers now smeared with red soil. He picks up his bat and nods calmly toward Javeed.

ANJI
Good carry. Chusava Suresh anna? Carry chusava?

SURESH
Moham meedhaki ochindi kada ra.

ANJI
Bounce pitch nunchi extract chesadu. Good ball. Leaving is also an art. Test cricket lo adhe main.

BABU
(veins bulging on his neck)
Rey! Leaving enduku ra, padi sachav ground meedha!

ANJI
(raising a palm, sternly)
Evadanna body balance lose aithe duck chestharu Babu. Blind ga bat thippithe slip lo catch pothadi. Next ball chusko.

Anji walks back into his crease, but his legs are visibly trembling. He glances at the field. He looks at Javeed, who is already jogging back to the top of his run-up, humming a song.

Anji knows he cannot survive another delivery. His brain races.

Anji quickly walks halfway down the pitch, waving his hand toward Babu.

ANJI
Babu, listen. Simple math. Nuvvu left-hander vi ga, vadu off-stump outside vese chances unnay. Nenu single theesi istha. Nuvvu strike theesko.

BABU
Neeku strike ivvadam istam leka kada ra intasepu kottindi? Ippudu kotha ball raagane naaku isthava?

ANJI
Team mukhyam Babu! Selfish ga aadalenu nenu.

BABU
Nee paadaalaki dhandam ra, single theesi edavaku, nannu runout chesthav nuvvu.

Javeed runs in again. High arm action.

He drops it short of length, angling in fast.

Anji closes his eyes, shuffles awkwardly outside leg stump, and just hangs his bat out defensively like an umbrella.

*THUD.*

The hard ball ricochets off the bottom edge, rolling merely three feet away from the pitch, right next to the bowler's follow-through.

ANJI
(without even looking where the ball is)
YES! YES! RUNNNNN BABU!

Anji takes off like a man fleeing a burning building, sprinting toward the non-striker end with his head down.

BABU
REY VADDU! BOWLER CHETHILONE UNDI RA—

ANJI
(screaming mid-stride)
BHAGOOOO!

Javeed turns around, sees Anji already at the bowler's stumps, and rushes to pick up the ball.

Babu has no choice. He curses loudly and dives headfirst toward the batting crease.

Javeed picks up the ball and aims at the stumps—*MISSES.* The ball rolls away toward deep square leg.

Babu is lying horizontally on the pitch, face full of red dust, his hawai chappal broken in two.

SURESH
Not out! Over throw!

Anji is already standing at the non-striker end, adjusting his sweatband, completely unfazed.

ANJI
(clapping his hands)
Good call! Running between the wickets ante adhi! Pressure create chesthe fieldsmen thadabadatharu.

Babu slowly pushes himself off the mat. He looks at his broken chappal, then looks at Anji with eyes full of murder.

BABU
(panting, voice trembling with rage)
Over throw lo second run theeyaledhe ra nuvvu?

ANJI
Calculated risk Babu. Striker end lo unte neeku free ga shot aade angle dhorukuthadi. Nine balls, twelve runs. Match mana chethilo undi. Nuvvu calm ga aadu.

Babu spits mud out of his mouth, limps back to the crease, and grips his bat with white knuckles.

Javeed walks past Anji back to his mark, smirking.

JAVEED
Babu bhai ni champesettu unnav ga Anji?

ANJI
(looking away, serious)
Intent undali Javeed. Cricket lo commitment unnodike runs osthay. You bowl now.
beat_summary: Anji mistimes a defensive shot and immediately blames the ball's internal weight and seam compression to cover his poor stroke.
Javeed calls his bluff and offers a brand-new, hard Nivia tennis ball, causing Babu to panic because it gives the bowler a dangerous bouncer advantage.
Anji insists on taking the new ball out of misplaced pride, forcing Babu into a rage over their match fee and safety.
Javeed bowls a fast bouncer; Anji completely loses his nerve, drops his bat, and falls flat on his back to dodge it.
Anji recovers and absurdly praises the ball's carry and his own 'test cricket' leave, infuriating Babu further.
Trapped by his own fear of facing another delivery, Anji forces a panicked single onto Babu, leading to an awkward overthrow scramble and Babu's chappal breaking.
Anji calmly congratulates his own tactical brilliance while Babu stands ready to murder him on the pitch.

scene:
**BLACK SCREEN**

Slow, intensely sorrowful cello music plays. 

OLD NARRATOR (V.O.)
*(Deep, dramatic, like a 1980s tragedy)*
Yuvatha... Aashalu, aaveshaala madhya nalipe oka tharam. Lakshyanni vadilesi, premayana maayaa-valamlo padi, jeevithaaniki daari theliyaka thalladille oka niraashaakaara yuvakudi gaadha idhi...

*RECORD SCRATCH.* The tragic music cuts out dead.

KARTHIK (V.O.)
Anna! Aagu anna. Rey... chethulu jodistha konchem aa microwave sound lanti music aaputhara mundhu?

A clumsy microphone thud. Someone coughs.

KARTHIK (V.O.)
*(to the audience, completely conversational)*
Evadu anna niraashaakari? Asalu evarki chepthunnav ee story? Em cinema dialogue lu bro ivi... 

Silence for a beat.

KARTHIK (V.O.)
Maa nanna friend okadu unnadu lendi. Doordarshan lo documentary lu chesevaadu anta. Mic kanipisthe chalu, direct ga depressing mood loki vellipothadu. Meeru vadini nammakandi. Idhi antha pedda thop canvas story em kaadhu. 

**EXT. RTC BUS STOP - VIDYANAGAR - DAY (2017)**

Sweaty, chaotic afternoon. 

Yellow TSRTC buses spewing black smoke. Hundreds of intermediate boys in sky-blue striped shirts and navy-blue trousers pushing past each other like a stampede.

KARTHIK (V.O.)
Idi 2017. WhatsApp lo blue-tick lu kothaga vachi, manushula madhya unna konchem prashaanthathanu kuda chedadobbinchina rojulu avi. Appatlo phone lo 1GB 3G net pack ante... gold biscuit tho samanam.

Amidst the crowd, KARTHIK (17) stands near an iron pillar. 

His uniform shirt is half-tucked in. His hair is set with an excessive amount of Parachute coconut oil, rigidly combed to the side. He is holding a spiral-bound physics record book against his chest like an armor.

KARTHIK (V.O.)
Idhigo... ee photo frame lo kurchunna vaadike gaadu... nene. Karthik. Sri Chaitanya, Vidyanagar branch. MPC Section C-4. Ante... marks batti chusthe college lo border security force lanti vallam memu. Ee roju nunchi repatiki fail avvakunda unte chaalu ane batch.

Karthik suddenly straightens up. He wipes his sweaty forehead with the back of his hand, checks his reflection in the rusted bus-stop ad, and slicks his oily hair down again.

KARTHIK (V.O.)
Kaani naaku oka vishayam lo chala balamaina confidence undedi. Marks raakapothe em? Personality undi ga. Mana range veru ani na gundello nenu fix aypoya.

Through the crowd, walking toward the women's queue—

SNEHA (17). 

Neatly pleated uniform, huge black backpack strapped tightly across both shoulders, holding a laminated Formula Sheet in one hand and reading it while walking. Totally unaware of the world around her.

KARTHIK (V.O.)
Aame Sneha. Section A-1. Desk meeda rendu highlighters, moodu ball pens pettukuni, lunch break lo kuda integration problems solve chese rakam. 

Sneha stops, tucks a strand of hair behind her ear, and highlights a line on the sheet without missing a step.

KARTHIK (V.O.)
Maa iddari madhya common point enti thelusa? Ma iddarki maths lecturer gadu ante istam undadu. Kani theda enti ante... aame ki vadu cheppedi slow anipisthadi, naku vadu cheppedi Telugu lo unna kooda ardham kaadhu.

Karthik takes a deep breath, clears his throat, and walks toward the queue with deliberate, rehearsed swagger.

KARTHIK (V.O.)
Science lo oka principle undi... opposites attract ani. Evado peddamanishi textbook lo raasadu. Vadi meeda nammakam tho, nenu aame attention kottadaniki oka master plan vesa.

Karthik casually steps right into Sneha’s walking path, pretending to look deeply into the sky like he’s pondering the cosmos.

KARTHIK (V.O.)
Plan simple. Casual ga thagilipovali. Book kindapadi povali. Nenu sorry cheppi theesi ivvali. Simple eye contact, slight smile, chemistry begins.

Sneha approaches. Karthik subtly angles his shoulder to clip hers.

Sneha, still reading the laminated sheet, cleanly side-steps him by two inches without even looking up. 

Karthik, having committed his full momentum into thin air, trips over his own untied Bata shoe lace and goes crashing sideways straight into a roadside sugarcane juice cart.

*CLATTER.* Metal tumblers bounce across the pavement.

Sneha board the bus calmly, punching her bus pass with the conductor.

The juice vendor stares down at Karthik, who is now flat on the ground, sticky with crushed sugarcane pulp.

KARTHIK (V.O.)
Physics fail ayyindi kani... ma katha akkade modhalaindi.
beat_summary: An old dramatic narrator opens the story with a tragic, over-the-top voiceover about youth and despair.
Karthik aggressively interrupts the old narrator, calling out his cliché tone and dismissing his depressing documentary style.
The setting shifts to a chaotic Vidyanagar bus stop in 2017, with intermediate students swarming in uniforms.
Karthik introduces himself as an average, oil-slicked Sri Chaitanya MPC student surviving on pure misplaced confidence and personality.
Sneha is introduced as a hyper-studious, focused section A-1 student totally absorbed in her formulas.
Karthik devises a simple, confident master plan to casually collide with her and drop his physics record book to spark instant chemistry.
Karthik executes his approach, but Sneha effortlessly side-steps him without looking up from her sheet.
Karthik’s momentum carries him into a sugarcane juice cart, tripping over his untied shoelace and landing flat in the pulp while Sneha boards her bus unbothered.

scene:
**INT. RAHUL’S BEDROOM - MORNING**

Dead silence. No traffic hum. No distant pressure cooker whistles. Nothing.

RAHUL (31) jerks upright in bed, chest heaving. His T-shirt is soaked at the collar. He stares at his hands—fingers rigid, knuckles white. 

He blinks against the pale morning light filtering through the sheer curtains. 

On the bedside table, his phone screen is black. He taps it. Nothing. Dead.

Rahul swings his legs off the bed. The mosaic floor is ice-cold under his bare feet.

**INT. LIVING ROOM / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS**

The apartment is spotless. Too neat. 

At the open kitchen counter, RADHIKA (29) stands with her back to him, stirring something in a steel saucepan over the stove. The flame is a silent blue hiss.

Rahul stops in the hallway, gripping the doorframe.

RAHUL
Radhika?

Radhika turns around. Fresh face, hair pinned up loosely, wearing a faded cotton kurti. She gives him an easy, familiar smile.

RADHIKA
Lechava? Chala sepu padukunnav. Coffee pedthunna, rendu nimishalu kurcho.

Rahul rubs his temples. A dull throb behind his eyes.

RAHUL
Time entha? Phone on avvatledhu.

RADHIKA
(pouring milk into the pan)
Seven-thirty ala avthundi. Chargo pettuko, switch board loose undi kada.

Rahul walks toward the balcony sliding glass door. 

He pulls it open. 

Outside, the street below is frozen in gray morning mist. A stray dog stands mid-stride on the asphalt. An auto-rickshaw is parked near the gate, driver seated inside with his hands on the handlebar, staring straight ahead. Not a single leaf on the neem tree is moving.

No sound enters the room. Absolute vacuum.

Rahul takes a half-step back, his heart knocking against his ribs.

RAHUL
Radhika... bayata traffic sound emi ledu enti? 

Radhika doesn't look up from the stove. She turns off the flame with a click.

RADHIKA
Sunday kada Rahul. Andaru padukuntaru ga ee time lo.

RAHUL
Sunday enti? Ninna Thursday kada? Nenu office nunchi vachi... cab book cheskuni...

He trails off. He tries to remember coming home. The memory is completely flat, like a blank wall.

Radhika picks up two steel tumblers of filter coffee and walks to the small dining table. She places one in front of an empty chair and pushes a small plastic container toward it.

RADHIKA
Kurcho mundhu. Coffee challaripothundi.

Rahul slowly walks to the table, eyes fixed on her. He pulls the chair back. The scrape of the chair legs against the floor makes no sound at all. 

He freezes. 

Radhika sits opposite him, calmly blowing on her coffee.

RADHIKA
Em chusthav ala? Thaagu.

Rahul looks down at the table. In front of him, next to his tumbler, sits a bowl of white sugar and a steel spoon. 

RAHUL
Nuvvu sugar eyyaledha?

RADHIKA
(smiling slightly)
Nuvve kada epudu moodu spoons eskuntav. Nenu veste thakkuva aypothadi antav.

Rahul looks at the sugar bowl. Then at her.

RAHUL
Radhika... naku diabetes detect ayyi three years ayyindi. Sugar muttukonu nenu.

Radhika’s smile doesn’t drop. It just stays there, perfectly fixed.

RADHIKA
Em matladuthunnav Rahul? Ee madhya prathi daaniki overthink chesthunnav. Nuvvu, sugar thinnakapovadam enti? Roju veskuntav ga.

RAHUL
(voice tightening)
Roju eyyadam enti? Radhika, serious ga matladuthunna. Nenu sugar teeskonu. Asalu phone enduku pani cheyatledhu? And where is the dog? Mana Jimmy ekkada?

Radhika takes a slow sip of her coffee. Sets the tumbler down with deliberate care.

RADHIKA
Jimmy evaru?

Rahul stares at her. His throat tightens.

RAHUL
Mana kukka, Radhika. Last year adoption center nunchi thechamu. Jimmy. Black Labrador. Ekkada vadu?

Radhika looks at him with genuine, patient concern. The kind of look one gives a sick child.

RADHIKA
Rahul... manaki pets ante padadhu. Neeku dust allergy kada. Asalu manam eppudu kukkani penchaledhu.

RAHUL
(standing up abruptly)
Pichi matalu matladaku! Hall lo vadi belt undedi... aa corner lo vadi bowl undedi!

Rahul turns toward the corner near the shoe rack. 

Empty. Just plain white skirting board. No scuffs, no bowl, no scratches on the wall.

Rahul backing away from the table, breathing heavily.

RAHUL
Nenu... nenu inka nidralone unna. This is a dream. Nenu inka levaledhu.

RADHIKA
(softly, remaining seated)
Dream aithe nenu neetho enduku matladathanu?

RAHUL
Because my brain is making you say it! Nuvvu real kadhu. Ee room real kadhu. 

Radhika slowly stands up. She doesn't look angry. She looks slightly exhausted, like they have had this exact conversation ten times already.

RADHIKA
Sare. Nenu real kadhu anuko. Mari ee flat evaridhi?

RAHUL
Manadhi. Manam rent ki theskunnam.

RADHIKA
Address cheppu.

Rahul opens his mouth. 

Nothing comes out. 

He knows the road. He knows the lane. But the building name, the flat number, the area—vanished. A total void.

Rahul’s hands start to shake. He grabs the edge of the dining table. 

RAHUL
Nidralo unna nenu... Radhika, please. Just wake me up. Nannu shake cheyi, leda water kottu moham meeda. Just do something!

Radhika walks around the table toward him. Her footsteps make no sound on the tiles. 

She stops just inches away. She reaches up, her fingers cool, and gently touches his cheek.

Her skin feels real. Her warmth feels real.

RADHIKA
(whispering, gentle)
Rahul... okkasari mirror lo chusko.

Rahul’s eyes widen.

RAHUL
Enti?

RADHIKA
Washbasin daggarki velli moham chusko. Neeke ardham avthundi.

Rahul stares at her eyes. Her pupils are wide, dark, reflecting nothing. Not the light, not the room, not even his own face.

Trembling, Rahul backs away from her toward the hallway bathroom.

He steps inside. 

He grips the ceramic sink with both hands. He slowly raises his head to look into the mirror.

The mirror reflects the empty bathroom. The tiles. The open door behind him. Radhika standing in the doorway, watching him quietly.

The mirror reflects everything in the room.

Except Rahul.
beat_summary: Rahul wakes up in a silent, dead apartment and finds his phone dead.
Radhika stands in the kitchen, casually making coffee and behaving normally.
Rahul steps onto the balcony and discovers the outside world is completely frozen and soundless.
Radhika dismisses his concerns as a normal Sunday, ignoring the reality of the day and date.
Rahul's memories begin to dissolve when he tries to recall how he got home and his address.
Radhika questions him about household details like his sugar consumption and a pet dog, claiming they never had one and he has no allergies.
Rahul realizes he is dreaming and begs Radhika to wake him up.
Radhika tells him to look in the bathroom mirror.
Rahul looks into the bathroom mirror and sees the entire room reflected, but he casts no reflection at all.

scene:
**EXT. GATED COMMUNITY PENTHOUSE - TERRACE - NIGHT**

Zero breeze. The distant hum of the Outer Ring Road. 

A quiet, candlelit wooden table against the parapet wall. Two half-eaten takeaway shawarmas wrapped in silver foil. 

POOJA (24) leans back on the wrought-iron chair, looking out at the city skyline. She looks genuinely happy, her guard down.

VINAY (26) sits opposite her in a freshly ironed linen shirt, rolling up his sleeves with practiced nonchalance. He smiles, tapping his foot.

POOJA
(softly)
Nijamga Vinay... nenu nammalekapothunna. Your friend gave you the terrace key just like that? Ila midnight view kosam?

VINAY
(smiles, waving a hand)
Arre, Akhil gadu naku chaddi dosth Pooja. US vellipoye mundhu flat keys na chethilo petti, 'Vinay, eppudu peace kaavalanna velli chill avvu' annadu. Manaki circle alantidi. Manam adagalsina avasaram ledhu, vaalle istharu.

Pooja looks at him, eyes soft. She reaches across the small table and puts her hand over his. 

Vinay freezes for half a second, his chest swelling with quiet triumph.

POOJA
Thank you. Nenu eppudu ninnu edho oka vishayam lo judge chesthu untanu kada... but this is really sweet. Nuvvu show-off kadhu ani ippude thelusthundi.

Vinay clears his throat, heart hammering for a totally different reason.

VINAY
Manam eppudu simple Pooja. Edho nee kosam oka special—

*CLACK.*

Downstairs. Inside the flat. The heavy metallic thud of the front door latch opening.

Vinay’s mouth snaps shut. His spine goes rigid.

Pooja pulls her hand back, frowning.

POOJA
Adhi... kinda sound vachindi?

VINAY
(forcing a grin, eyes wide)
Ledu... gali vachuntadi. Curtains kottukuni untay.

*CLICK. HUMMM.*

A split second later, warm yellow light floods the stairwell leading up to the terrace. Through the frosted glass door, heavy footsteps echo against marble tiles.

A middle-aged man’s hoarse voice drifts up:

MAN (O.S.)
(talking on phone downstairs)
Ha Sharma garu, reach aypoyam. Flight one hour early ga land aindi. Ten minutes lo fresh up ayyi documents pampistha.

Vinay’s face drains of all color. His lips part, but no sound comes out.

Pooja stares at him, her voice dropping to a harsh whisper.

POOJA
Vinay... evaru vadu? Nee friend US lo untadu annav ga?

VINAY
(whispering, trembling)
Ha... vadu... Akhil gadu kadhu idi. Valla babai anukunta. Sudden ga... keys theeskuni...

POOJA
Babai enti Vinay?! Nuvvu Akhil gadi flat annav!

MAN (O.S.)
(louder, closer to the stairs)
Rey Suresh! Terrace light evadu on chesi pettadu ra? Meter bill evadu kadathadu?

The footsteps begin pounding heavily up the wooden steps. *Thud. Thud. Thud.*

Pooja grabs her handbag from the chair, sheer panic in her eyes. Vinay snatches the two half-eaten shawarmas, desperately looking for a place to throw them, before stuffing them awkwardly inside his own laptop bag.

VINAY
(frantic whisper)
Corner ki ra... aa water tank venakki ra mundhu!

They scramble across the rough stone floor, crouching low behind a massive Sintex water tank. Pooja’s knee scrapes against the brick wall. She ignores the pain, her breath hitching.

Through the glass terrace door, a bald, heavy-set MAN in a safari suit steps out into the night. He carries a brass key bunch and a thick wooden walking stick.

The Man stops. He squints at the table.

The candle is still burning, wax dripping onto the table.

Behind the tank, Vinay and Pooja are pressed tight against the damp wall. Their faces are inches apart. Vinay’s chest is heaving violently, sweat dripping down his temple onto his collar.

Pooja looks down at Vinay’s shaking hand. 

He is clutching the bunch of keys he used to let them into the building. Hanging from the iron ring is a laminated barcode tag with red bold text:

*NOBROKER HOURLY INSPECTION UNIT - AGENT: VINAY KUMAR (RETURN BY 8:00 PM).*

Pooja stares at the tag. 

Her eyes slowly lift to his face. The romance from two minutes ago is completely, utterly dead.

POOJA
(in a razor-sharp, furious whisper)
Idhi Akhil flat kaadha?

Vinay swallows hard. His throat makes an audible click. He covers his face with one hand, his whisper cracking with shame.

VINAY
Pooja... please... ippudu kadhu...

POOJA
Nuvvu inspection boy va? Vere valla flat keys theeskuni nannu date ki thechava ra daddamma?!

VINAY
(desperate, eyes pleading)
Fifty-thousand rent flat idhi Pooja! Oka coffee shop lo kurchunte neeku special anipinchadhu ani... chusthavu ani...

POOJA
Chachav na chethilo! Vadu police ki call chesthe ma intlo em cheppali ra bewakoof?!

Out on the terrace, the Man mutters a curse. 

MAN (O.S.)
Candle evadu pettadu ikkada? Pilla na kodukulu... donga na dash gallu...

The Man’s heavy slippers scrape against the gravel. He walks directly toward the water tank, raising his stick.

Vinay looks at Pooja. His eyes are terrified, but something stubborn and guilty takes over. He slips off his Bata slip-ons silently.

VINAY
(whispering, voice shaking)
Pooja. Nen bayataki velli vadi mundhu parigedatha. Vadu na venaka vasthadu. Nuvvu ventane stairwell nunchi kindhaki vellipo. Lift vaddu, steps nunchi vellu.

Pooja freezes. Her anger halts for a split second as she sees his face—pale, humiliated, completely ready to get beaten with a stick just to clear the path for her.

POOJA
Vinay... vaddu... vadu kodathadu ninnu—

VINAY
Naku alavate. Nuvvu bayatapadali. That's it.

Before she can grab his collar, Vinay lunges out from behind the tank, barefoot, holding his laptop bag over his head like a shield.

VINAY
(screaming like a madman)
AYYO GHOST! DHEYYAM UNNAYIKKADAAAA!

The safari-suit Man jumps two feet in the air, dropping his stick with a clatter.

MAN
Arey! Evadra nuvvu—

Vinay doesn't look back. He sprints past the Man, deliberately knocking over an empty flower pot with a deafening *CRASH*, and bolts down the fire exit stairs into the dark.

MAN
(chasing him, panting)
Aagura lathkor na kodaka! Security! Gate veyyandi ra!

Their chaotic shouting echoes down the stairwell, fading away into the floors below.

Silence falls back over the terrace.

Pooja remains behind the tank, breathing heavily in the dark, gripping her handbag with white knuckles. 

On the floor in front of her lies Vinay’s left shoe. He ran so fast he left it behind.

A beat. 

She picks up the dirty shoe, wipes her face with the back of her hand, and mutters under her breath:

POOJA
Pichi vedhava.

She slips out toward the stairs.
beat_summary: Vinay brings Pooja to a luxury penthouse terrace for a date, pretending his friend lent it to him.
Pooja lets her guard down and touches his hand, praising him for not being a show-off.
A middle-aged man unexpectedly enters the flat below, turning out to be an occupant/relative rather than Vinay's friend.
Vinay and Pooja frantically hide behind a water tank as the man comes up to the terrace.
Pooja discovers a NoBroker hourly inspection barcode tag on Vinay's keys, realizing he is an inspection agent using a client's flat for a date.
The safari-suit man approaches their hiding spot, prompting Vinay to sacrifice himself by screaming 'ghost' and bolting to draw the man away.
Pooja is left behind in the dark, finding Vinay's left shoe, and mutters 'Pichi vedhava' as she escapes.

scene:
**INT. SUMATHI’S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EVENING**

A cramped hall in an old Malkajgiri house. The low drone of a pedestal fan oscillates against the peeled green wall paint. 

TEJA (8) sits on the carpet, transfixed by a glossy red remote-control car. The headlights flash blue and red across the floor tiles. 

On the sofa above him sits VENKAT (42). Safari suit, a thick gold ring on his pinky finger, smelling of Mysore Sandal soap and pan masala. He watches the boy with an easy, lingering smile.

VENKAT
Speed baagunda Teja?

TEJA
(eyes wide, gripping the plastic remote)
Chala fast pothundi Babanji! Road meedha kooda run avthada?

VENKAT
Road meedhane running. Kinda mana bullet bike meedha petti, key niku istha. Padha, kindaki veldam. 

Teja scrambles up, ready to sprint out.

SUMATHI (34) steps out from the kitchen carrying a steel tumbler of lukewarm tea. Her hair is loosely pinned, saree pallu tucked into her waist, her forearms dusted with dry flour. 

She stops at the doorway. Her eyes flick from the red toy to Venkat’s hand resting casually near Teja’s shoulder.

SUMATHI
Chai theeskondi bava.

Venkat doesn’t reach for the tea immediately. He leans forward, resting his elbows on his knees.

VENKAT
Maradhalu... Teja ni bayataki theskelthunna. Just aa Chilkalguda bridge daaka velli, ice cream thipinchi thestha. Araganta.

TEJA
(jumping)
Amma, bullet meedha anta! Please nenu potha!

Sumathi places the tea tumbler on the teapoy with a soft, deliberate click. She does not look at Venkat. 

SUMATHI
Velladu.

Venkat chuckles, shaking his head.

VENKAT
Enduku maradhalu? Choodu, vadu entha excited unnaado. Pillalani illallo petti lock chesthe em ఎదుగుతారు? Manam unnam ga chuskodaniki.

SUMATHI
(calm, flat)
Homework inka poorthi kaaledhu. Repu unit test undi.

TEJA
Amma! Test Monday kada! Repu Sunday!

Sumathi looks directly at Teja. Her gaze is steady, devoid of anger, but completely unmovable. 

SUMATHI
Teja. Bag theesi maths table meedha pettu. Ippude vasthunna.

TEJA
(whining, stomping his foot)
Prathi saari anthe nuvvu! Babanji pilusthunte enduku apthav? Roju intlone kurchovala nenu?

Venkat smiles, stretching his arm out toward the boy’s head.

VENKAT
Parledhu le ra, valla amma ki bayam ekkuva. Chinnapudu mee nanna kuda itlane bayapadevadu maa nanna ante. Nene kurchobetti anni nerpincha. (looks up at Sumathi) Pilladiki eppudo okappudu teliyali kada maradhalu, bayata prapancham ela untado? Nenu daggara undi chuskunta kada... vere evaro kaadhu ga.

Sumathi steps in smoothly, angling her body directly between Venkat’s outstretched hand and Teja. The reach is broken.

SUMATHI
Maa prapancham intlo varake baava. Bayataki vachi nerchukovalsina avasaram vadiki inka raledhu. 

Venkat’s smile stiffens at the edges. His fingers curl back slowly.

VENKAT
Sare. Nee ishtam. Kani maree antha tight ga petti penchaku. Tharvatha vadike chethilo nunchi jaari poyina feeling vasthadi.

He picks up the tea tumbler, takes a small sip, and sets it back down.

VENKAT (CONT'D)
Nenu vastha mari. Thammudu vachaka cheppu, shop daggara wait chesthunta ani.

Venkat picks up his helmet from the teapoy, glances at Teja one last time, and walks toward the main door. 

The door clicks shut behind him.

Teja stands by the wall, tears prickling in his eyes, furiously holding the plastic remote.

TEJA
Nuvvu asalu manchidanivi kaavu Amma. Epudu intlane untav, nannu kooda ekkadiki ponivvavu. Nenu Babanji tho matladanu inka, neetho kooda matladanu!

Teja throws the remote on the carpet and storms into the bedroom, slamming the door halfway shut.

Sumathi stands in the center of the quiet hall. The red toy car on the floor continues to flash its tiny blue and red LEDs in the dimming twilight.

She walks over. She picks up the toy car, switches off the small black slider at the bottom, and sets it on the shelf, out of reach.

**INT. BEDROOM - CONTINUOUS**

The room is dark except for the streetlight filtering through the rusted window grill.

Teja is curled up sideways on the narrow cot, his back turned to the door, staring bitterly at the wall, sniffing quietly.

The mattress dips slightly as Sumathi sits on the edge beside him. 

Teja immediately stiffens, pulling his knees closer to his chest to shut her out.

Sumathi doesn't speak. She doesn't explain the door she just closed. She doesn't tell him why that car was bought, or what kind of silence lives in houses where men like Venkat are allowed to be generous.

She just sits there.

Slowly, she takes the damp corner of her cotton saree pallu. She reaches over and gently pulls his small, clenched right hand into hers. 

Teja resists for a second, then lets his fingers go limp with stubborn resentment.

With slow, rhythmic strokes, Sumathi quietly wipes away the sticky sweet syrup left on his small fingers from the laddu Venkat had handed him at the door—rubbing his skin completely clean, over and over, until nothing of the man remains on the boy.
beat_summary: Venkat gives Teja a flashy remote-control car and entices him with a motorbike ride to get ice cream.
Sumathi interrupts by offering tea, casually blocking Venkat's request to take Teja out under the guise of pending homework.
Venkat attempts to overrule her by dismissing her caution, but Sumathi firmly interposes herself between his hand and Teja.
Venkat backs down with a mild passive-aggressive warning about over-protection and leaves the house.
Teja throws a temper tantrum, blames Sumathi for ruining his fun, and storms into the bedroom.
Sumathi quietly puts away the toy car, goes into the dark room, and meticulously cleans the sticky sweet syrup off Teja's fingers.

scene:
**INT. LATHA'S APARTMENT - LIVING ROOM - AFTERNOON**

The steady *whir* of an old ceiling fan cuts through the quiet. Sunlight angles through the balcony grill, laying zebra stripes of shadow across the mosaic floor.

ROHIT (7) sits cross-legged on a faded coir mat, bent over an open drawing book, carefully coloring an apple with a red wax crayon.

On the sofa, PRAVEEN (38) leans back. Clean-shaven, crisp linen shirt, legs crossed comfortably. He holds an empty ceramic teacup with both hands, watching Rohit.

LATHA (32) walks in from the kitchen carrying a stainless steel water jug. Her saree pallu is tucked neatly into her waist. She sets the jug down on the small center table.

LATHA
Chai inkonchem teesukuntara, Praveen bava?

PRAVEEN
(smiling, soft tone)
Chaalu Latha, baga pettav. Madhu inka raaledha? Juice thevadaniki antha sepa?

LATHA
Supermarket lo crowd untadi kada. Osthadu.

Praveen sets the empty cup on the glass table. He leans forward, elbows on his knees, closing the distance between himself and Rohit.

PRAVEEN
Rohit-u.

Rohit doesn’t look up immediately. He keeps scribbling inside the red lines.

PRAVEEN (CONT'D)
Rohit. Choodu ikkada.

Rohit raises his head, crayon still touching the paper.

PRAVEEN (CONT'D)
(tapping the sofa cushion beside him)
Akkada kindha enduku kurchunnav? Ikkadiki raa. Ra, sofa meeda kurcho. Phone lo car racing game undi, theesi istha.

Praveen pulls out his smartphone, unlocks it, and tilts the screen so the boy can see the bright colors. 

Rohit looks at the phone, then glances toward the kitchen door instinctively. He starts to get up.

Latha steps forward. Her movement is calm, completely unhurried, but deliberate. 

She walks directly between the sofa and the mat, cutting the line of sight. She bends down, picking up an empty plastic glass from the floor right near Rohit's feet.

LATHA
Rohit, hand wash cheskuni vellu. Hands motham wax antukundi choodu.

Rohit looks at his palms.

ROHIT
Ledhu Amma, crayon dust anthe—

LATHA
(firm, gentle, without looking back)
Bathroom ki velli soap tho kadukko ra. Velli.

PRAVEEN
(chuckling quietly)
Pillodni prathi daaniki visigisthav enduku Latha? Daggarki pilisthe hand wash antav. Roju illantlone untadu kada.

Praveen extends his right arm, fingers open, gesturing for Rohit to bypass his mother.

PRAVEEN (CONT'D)
Ikkadaki ra Rohit. Mee Amma thone untav rojantha. Bava daggarki ra.

Rohit hesitates, caught between them. He takes a half-step toward Praveen's outstretched hand.

Latha doesn’t raise her voice. She doesn’t flinch. 

She takes one step to the right, fully occupying the gap. Her body completely blocks Rohit from Praveen's view.

She reaches down, takes Rohit by the upper arm—not roughly, but with a secure, anchoring grip—and turns him toward the hallway.

LATHA
Bed meeda nee school bag open chesi undi Rohit. Tomorrow's timetable set cheyi. Nenu vachi chustha.

ROHIT
Amma, game aadatha—

LATHA
Lopalki vellu nana.

Her voice carries a flat, unyielding weight. Rohit senses it. He drops the red crayon onto the mat and jogs down the narrow corridor toward the bedroom.

The bedroom door creaks as it pushes open, followed by the soft rustle of school notebooks.

Silence returns to the living room, filled only by the rhythmic hum of the fan.

Praveen’s outstretched hand remains suspended in the air for a second. Slowly, his fingers curl inward. He lowers his hand and leans back into the sofa, resting his arm along the backrest.

His smile hasn't left his face, but his eyes stay fixed on Latha. Cold, evaluating.

PRAVEEN
(casual)
Madhu cheppadu le. Nuvvu konchem over-protective ani. 

Latha doesn't answer immediately. She bends down, picks up Rohit’s drawing book, and snaps it shut. She picks up the scattered crayons one by one, dropping them into their little plastic box.

LATHA
Madhu ki thelidhu bava. Pillalu entha careful ga unna saripodhu ee madhya.

PRAVEEN
Mana sontha vaalla daggara kuda na?

He tilts his head, watching her face for a crack. 

Latha stands up straight, holding the drawing book and crayon box against her chest. She meets his eyes directly. Her expression is completely devoid of warmth, but entirely polite.

LATHA
Evvaraina anthe. 

A scooter engine rumbles outside the gate, followed by a brief honk. Madhu’s voice can be heard downstairs talking to the watchman.

Praveen shifts slightly, glancing toward the balcony, then back at Latha.

PRAVEEN
Madhu vachinattu unnadu.

LATHA
Avunu.

She doesn't wait for him to stand. She doesn't offer to take his teacup.

Latha turns and walks down the hallway. 

She reaches the bedroom door. Rohit is sitting on the edge of the mattress, pulling a notebook from his school bag.

Latha steps inside, reaches behind her, and quietly pulls the heavy teak door shut until the latch clicks firmly into the brass frame. 

She doesn't bolt it. She just stands there against the closed door, her back flat against the wood, holding the handle in place with both hands.
beat_summary: Rohit sits on a mat coloring while Praveen sits on the sofa watching him, and Latha enters from the kitchen with a water jug.
Praveen dismisses Latha's offer of more chai and tries to lure Rohit over to the sofa with a smartphone game.
Latha physically steps between Praveen and Rohit, cutting their line of sight, and sends Rohit to wash his hands.
Praveen undermines Latha by calling her over-protective and aggressively extends his hand for Rohit to bypass her.
Latha calmly blocks Praveen again, grabs Rohit by the arm, and redirects him to his bedroom to work on his school timetable.
Rohit leaves, and Praveen drops his hand into a cold, evaluating posture while hinting that Madhu called her over-protective.
Latha quietly packs away the drawing materials, refusing to engage with his probing.
Madhu arrives downstairs, and Latha walks to the bedroom door, closing it and holding the handle from the inside to secure the space.

scene:
**INT. VENKAT RAO’S HOUSE - DINING AREA - NIGHT**

A bare 40-watt bulb hangs low over a small wooden dining table. 

The room is heavy with silence, punctured only by the uneven *clack-clack* of an old Usha table fan turning from side to side. 

VENKAT RAO (59) sits on a plastic chair, wearing a faded white banyan and a checked lungi. He eats rice and rasam with slow, mechanical efficiency. 

Across from him sits CHETAN (26). Chetan’s travel backpack leans against the wall behind him, still zipped shut, luggage tag still looped around the top handle. 

Chetan is not really eating. He uses his fingers to separate tiny pieces of curry leaves from his rice, lining them up neatly on the rim of his steel plate.

Venkat Rao reaches for the steel bowl in the middle of the table, scrapes the bottom with a spoon, and drops a small ladle of curd onto his own plate. He glances at Chetan.

Chetan’s eyes stay fixed on his plate.

VENKAT RAO
Perugu vesko.

CHETAN
Chalu nanna. Kadupu nindipoyindi.

VENKAT RAO
Rasam thone aypothadha? Annam migilchesav.

Venkat Rao doesn’t wait. He picks up the small bowl and tips the remaining curd straight onto the center of Chetan’s plate. 

A dull *plop*. 

Chetan looks at the white mound on his rice. He doesn’t protest. He quietly starts mixing it with his fingertips, his movements slow, deliberate.

On the corner of the table, Chetan’s phone screen lights up silently. 

A preview notification flashes: *“Final settlement processed. Relieving letter attached.”*

Chetan’s hand shifts slightly. Without breaking his rhythm, he pulls a paper napkin from the plastic holder and casually lays it over the phone screen, hiding the glow.

Venkat Rao has seen it. His chewing slows down for half a second. He doesn’t ask. He reaches for the steel tumbler, takes a measured sip of water, and wipes his wet mouth with the corner of the faded towel resting on his shoulder.

He turns his gaze toward the wall beside the front door.

A row of three brass hooks. 

The first hook holds an umbrella. The second holds Venkat Rao’s scooter key. 

The third hook is empty. On the peeling distemper wall around it, the dark, rectangular grease mark left by Chetan’s heavy bike keychain is clearly visible.

VENKAT RAO
Bandi shed lo pettava? Rendu rojula nunchi sandhu lo kanipiyatledu.

Chetan’s fingers stop moving in the curd rice. 

The table fan swivels toward them, blowing a weak, warm breeze across the table, then clicks and turns away.

CHETAN
(without looking up)
Adhi... friend theskelladu nanna. Service ki.

Silence stretches. 

Venkat Rao looks at Chetan’s hairline, the slight slump in his shoulders, the way his jaw is clenched tight enough to show the bone. 

Venkat Rao picks up a piece of mango pickle from his plate, places it in his mouth, and nods once.

VENKAT RAO
Sare.

Neither says another word. 

Venkat Rao finishes his meal, picks up his steel plate, and walks into the small kitchen. The sound of running tap water. The clink of steel against the granite sink.

Chetan sits alone at the table. He takes one mouthful of curd rice, swallows it dry, and stares down at his plate.

Venkat Rao walks out of the kitchen, wiping his wet hands on his towel. 

He doesn’t look at Chetan. He walks past the dining table to the old wooden cabinet beside the TV. He opens the top drawer. 

The soft rattle of loose safety pins, rubber bands, and old electricity receipts.

Venkat Rao reaches inside, picks up a spare key tied to a piece of faded red nylon twine—the key to his old 2008 Splendor.

He closes the drawer softly. 

He walks across the room toward the front door. 

Standing in front of the empty third hook, he lifts his arm and hangs the key on the brass peg. 

*Clink.*

The key sways slightly against the wall, then comes to a complete rest.

Venkat Rao turns off the dining room light, leaving only the hallway lamp on, and walks toward his bedroom.
beat_summary: Venkat Rao and Chetan eat dinner in heavy silence, punctuated by the oscillating table fan.
Venkat Rao forces extra curd onto Chetan's plate when Chetan tries to refuse food.
Chetan hides a work-termination notification on his phone beneath a paper napkin.
Venkat Rao notices the notification, pauses, and shifts his attention to the empty third brass hook where Chetan's bike key used to hang.
Venkat Rao asks about the bike; Chetan lies that a friend took it for service.
Venkat Rao accepts the lie quietly with a nod, finishes his meal, and goes to the kitchen.
Venkat Rao retrieves an old spare motorcycle key from the TV cabinet drawer.
Venkat Rao hangs the spare key on the empty third hook, turns off the dining light, and leaves Chetan alone in the fading light.

scene:
**INT. DINING ROOM - NIGHT**

A four-seater dining table with a faded floral plastic sheet. 

The ceiling fan wobbles slightly on speed three, ticking with every rotation: *tik... tik... tik.*

In the hallway corner, a grey VIP trolley bag stands upright. A backpack leans against it, zipped shut.

VENKAT (58) sits at the head of the table in a white banian and lungi. His reading glasses rest low on the bridge of his nose. He methodically mixes rice and tomato rasam on his steel plate, fingers working in small, quiet circles.

Opposite him sits VASU (25), wearing an old college t-shirt. His plate is barely touched. He breaks a papad into tiny, unnecessary pieces, piling the crumbs into a neat pyramid at the edge of his plate.

SAVITRI (52) emerges from the kitchen with a small steel bowl of curd. The hem of her saree is tucked at the waist. She sets the bowl between them, glancing between the two men.

SAVITRI
(low voice)
Annam inkonchem veyyana, Vasu?

VASU
Chalu amma. 

Vasu picks up the glass of water. Sips. Sets it down in the exact ring of moisture it left behind.

Venkat doesn’t look up. He reaches out for the curd bowl. His hand is steady, sun-spotted, knuckles thick from decades of desk work. He scoops two spoons of curd onto his rice.

VENKAT
Morning enni gantlaku train?

Vasu hesitates for half a second.

VASU
Six-forty. Secunderabad nunchi.

Venkat chews slowly. He takes a piece of lemon pickle from the rim of his plate, taps the excess oil against the edge, and places it on his tongue.

VENKAT
Platform two meedhaki vasthadi. Foot-over-bridge meedha escalator eppudu pani cheyadhu akkada. Luggage ekkuva undha?

VASU
Okkate bag. Heavy em ledhu.

VENKAT
Sare.

Silence returns. The fan ticks. *Tik... tik... tik.*

Savitri wipes the edge of the dining table with a damp cloth, lingering near Vasu’s chair.

SAVITRI
Morning tea ki lesthara? Five ki stove veligistha...

VENKAT
(cutting in, calm)
Auto dorakadhu antha early ga. App lo book chesthe drop out avtharu last minute lo. 

VASU
Main road varaku nadisthe share autos untay nanna. Nenu chuskunta.

Venkat’s fingers pause in his rice. Just for two beats. 

He doesn’t argue. He resumes mixing, scraping the bottom of the plate with the side of his thumb.

VENKAT
City vere ayna colony okate untadi anukoku. Bangalore lo language thelikapothe auto vadu chuttu thippi double theeskuntadu.

VASU
Office cab facility undi le. Flatmates kuda akkade untaru.

Venkat swallows. He wipes his hand against the side of his plate, then takes a sip of water. His eyes glance towards the hallway—at the VIP trolley bag—and then drop back to his plate.

VENKAT
Offer letter hard copy theeskellava?

VASU
Mail lo undi.

VENKAT
Printout theeyalsindi. Phone battery aypothe platform meedha evadiki chupisthav?

VASU
Company security daggara mail chupisthe saripothadi. Physical copy evaru adagaru ippudu.

Venkat stares at his fingers for a moment. He doesn't look convinced, but he lets it go.

VENKAT
Savitri, manchi neellu aypoyay.

Savitri quickly steps forward with the steel jug, filling his tumbler to the brim.

Venkat finishes the last bite. He pushes his chair back, the metal legs scraping loudly against the mosaic tiles. He stands, walks to the washbasin in the corner, and washes his hands. 

The tap water rushes into the sink, breaking the quiet. He dries his hands on the towel hanging by the nail, taking his time with each finger.

Vasu looks down at his plate. The food is cold. He quietly gathers the papad crumbs and pushes the plate slightly forward.

Venkat turns off the washbasin light. He walks past the dining table towards the hallway, his slippers slapping gently against the floor.

He stops beside the VIP trolley bag.

He looks down at it.

The top zipper isn't closed fully—about two inches remain open, showing the corner of a folded shirt.

Venkat stands there in the dim hall light. 

He bends down slowly, his knees making a faint crack. With two fingers, he takes the small zipper pull and slides it all the way to the end, tucking the metal tab firmly into its slot.

He straightens up, adjusts his lungi, and walks into his bedroom, leaving the door half-open.
beat_summary: Venkat and Vasu eat dinner in silence at the dining table while Savitri serves them.
Venkat questions Vasu about his train timings and travel logistics for Bangalore, masking his anxiety with practical advice.
Vasu brushes off his father's concerns about cabs, documents, and language barriers.
Venkat finishes eating, washes his hands at the sink, and walks toward the hallway.
Venkat stops by the packed VIP trolley bag and silently zips the remaining two inches fully shut before retiring to his room.

scene:
**INT. PRAKASH’S HOUSE - DINING AREA - NIGHT**

A four-seater dining table covered with a faded floral plastic sheet. 

The slow, rhythmic creak of the ceiling fan fills the room. On the small TV in the adjacent hall, a news channel plays on mute, blue light flickering across the lime-green wall.

PRAKASH (59) sits at his usual spot at the head of the table. Thin, silver-rimmed glasses, wearing a washed-out sleeveless banyan and a lungi. He eats slowly, mixing rasam and rice with measured, methodical finger movements. 

CHETAN (27) sits to his left. His hair is uncombed. He is staring down at his plate, pushing two pieces of fried potato around without putting them in his mouth. 

SUMATHI (53) walks out of the kitchen holding a steel bowl of curd. The hem of her cotton saree is tucked into her waist. She senses the silence, glances at Chetan, then places the bowl between them.

SUMATHI
Inkonchem annam pettana Chetu?

Chetan doesn't look up immediately.

CHETAN
Chaalu ma. 

Sumathi hesitates. She looks at Prakash. Prakash doesn’t look at either of them. He takes a small sip of water from his steel tumbler, sets it back down exactly where it was, and continues eating.

Beside Prakash's plate lies a brown paper courier envelope. Already torn open at the top. The white printed logo of an IT consultancy is visible on the upper corner. 

Chetan’s eyes keep drifting toward that envelope, then darting away.

CHETAN
(clearing his throat, low)
Ninna evening rain paddaka... hall lo fan sound ekkuvaindi. Repu electrician ni pilipistha.

Prakash chews silently. Five seconds pass.

PRAKASH
(flat, calm)
Avasaram ledhu. 

Prakash reaches out. His fingers, calloused from decades of bank ledger work, gently press against the brown envelope. 

He doesn't throw it. He just slides it across the plastic sheet until it touches the rim of Chetan’s water glass.

Sumathi stops moving. Her hand stays resting on the back of the empty chair.

Inside the envelope, Chetan can see the corner of the typed sheet: *RELIEVING ORDER & FULL SETTLEMENT.* Dated three weeks ago.

Chetan’s fingers freeze over his plate. The rice in his hand drops back onto the mound.

CHETAN
(voice tight, barely audible)
Adhi... nenu chepdam anukunna nanna. Project wrap up ayyindi. Next batch internal allocation lo undi, so—

PRAKASH
(without looking up)
Annam thinu mundhu.

Chetan stops mid-sentence. His throat works. 

Sumathi steps closer, her voice cautious, trying to soften the room.

SUMATHI
Next month vere company ki apply chestha annadu ga... Chetu, nuvvu curd vesko ra.

Prakash doesn't answer her. He carefully scrapes the last bit of rice from his plate, gathering it into a neat corner. 

PRAKASH
Roju poddunne ready ayyi laptop theeskuni ekkadiki velthunnav mari?

Chetan looks down at his lap. His hands are hidden under the table now.

CHETAN
KBR Park daggara... coffee shop lo kurchuntunna.

The ceiling fan clicks. Once. Twice.

Sumathi looks away, turning toward the kitchen counter, pretending to wipe a clean steel plate with a dry cloth. Her shoulders are rigid.

Prakash picks up his tumbler. Takes the last mouthful of water. He folds his hands over his stomach and looks at Chetan for the first time. Not angry. Just terribly tired, with eyes that have already run out of questions.

Prakash pushes his chair back slightly. The wooden legs scrape against the mosaic tiles with a dry screech.

Chetan quickly reaches out to take his father’s empty steel plate to carry it to the washbasin—an instinct to serve, to make up for something.

CHETAN
Nanna, aagandi... nenu thestha.

Prakash doesn't pull away. 

Instead, he slowly places his palm over Chetan’s hand, pressing it flat against the table. Firm, cool, unyielding.

Prakash holds it there for two seconds, keeping Chetan pinned in his seat.

Then, without taking his plate, Prakash stands up, turns, and walks slowly down the dimly lit hallway toward his bedroom, shutting the door behind him with a dull, quiet click.
beat_summary: Prakash and Chetan eat dinner in heavy silence while Sumathi tries to ease the atmosphere and offers food.
Prakash silently slides the opened IT consultancy relieving letter toward Chetan's water glass.
Chetan stammers an excuse about internal allocation, which Prakash cuts short by telling him to finish eating.
Prakash questions Chetan about where he goes every morning with his laptop, and Chetan admits he sits in a coffee shop near KBR Park.
Prakash finishes his water, places his palm flat over Chetan's hand to pin him in his seat, and walks away to his bedroom without taking his plate.

scene:
**EXT. CAMPUS quad - OAK TREE BENCH - AFTERNOON**

The four o'clock sun hits the stone bench. 

On a grease-stained piece of newspaper sitting between them lies **ONE** lonely, golden-brown samosa. Half-eaten chutney cups sit beside it.

VARUN (20) sits on the left, sleeves rolled up, arms crossed, staring intently at the samosa like a chess grandmaster evaluating a board.

ANANYA (19) sits on the right, clutching her college bag on her lap. She is staring at the exact same samosa with calm, unblinking focus.

A beat. Neither moves.

VARUN
(without looking at her)
Nuvvu lunch ki rendu chapathilu, full rice thinnav Ananya. Nenu chusa.

ANANYA
(equally calm)
Nuvvu canteen lo rendu Mirchi Bajji lu thintu naku kaniipinchav. Direct ga counter daggare నిలబడి thinnav. Memory thakkuva naku anukoku.

VARUN
Adhi finger food. Light snack. Main meal tho compare cheyakudadhu. Technically, nenu stomach space lo deficit lo unna ippudu.

ANANYA
Nee stomach budget gurinchi naku enduku? Samosa plate nenu order chesa.

VARUN
Gpay nene chesa ga!

ANANYA
Akkada network ledhani ninnu cheyyamanna. Hostel ki vellagaane rendu rupayila intrest tho saha pampistha. Money issue kadhu idi.

Ananya slowly extends her right index finger toward the newspaper. 

Varun instantly reaches out and taps her wrist away—not hard, just a quick blocking move.

VARUN
Rey... aagu. Fairness undali society lo. Rendu samosalu unnay plate lo. First dhi nuvvu ela thinnav? Quick ga, single bite lo complete chesav.

ANANYA
Nuvvu phone chusukuntu unnav. Cold aypothundi ani nenu thinna.

VARUN
Adhi opportunistic behaviour అంటారు. Nenu pause theeskunna. That doesn't mean I waived my right to the samosa.

Ananya tilts her head, looking at him with mild, amused disbelief.

ANANYA
Varun... oka 15 rupees samosa meeda thesis raasthunnav enti ra? 

VARUN
(shifting, posture straightening)
It's not about fifteen rupees. It's about proportion. Nuvvu modhati samosa lo 70% thinnav, cause corner crush ayyi kindha padipoyindi. So overall volume chusthe, nenu inka arrears lo unna.

ANANYA
Arrears ah? Engineering subjects thakkuva unnattu ikkada kuda arrears teesthunnava?

VARUN
Personal attacks vaddhu. Keep it clean.

Ananya sighs, adjusting her bag. She leans back slightly, switching tactics.

ANANYA
Sare. Nuvve thinu.

Varun blinks. He eyes her suspiciously.

VARUN
Em trick idi?

ANANYA
Trick em ledhu. Thinu. Edho nenu ninnu aakali thoni champesthunnattu aa look enti? Thinu, motham thinu.

VARUN
Nuvvu ala 'thinu' ani oka weird tone lo chepthe naku guilt vasthadi ani neeku thelusu.

ANANYA
Nenu normal gaane anna!

VARUN
Ledu, aa tone lo... 'Thinu, thinnaka nee conscience ninnu prashnisthadhii' ane hidden threat undi.

ANANYA
Arre babu, nenu em analedu! Samosa thinu ante itla kuda aalochisthara?

Varun looks down at the samosa. He hesitates. He reaches out, carefully pinches the corner of the crust, and lifts it two inches.

Ananya doesn't say a word. She just tracks the samosa with her eyes, her lips pressed into a tight, flat line.

Varun freezes mid-air.

VARUN
Chusa! Chusa aa look!

ANANYA
Nenu em chesa ippudu? Eye contact kuda cheyodha?

VARUN
Nuvvu కళ్లతోనే curse chesthunnav. Ee samosa thinte naku evening ki acidity vasthadhi, poyina subject lu thirigi vasthay.

ANANYA
(laughing despite herself)
Cha! Neeku overthinking ekkuva aypoyindi Varun. Give it here, nene saganamaaga cut chestha.

VARUN
Vaddhu. Nuvvu cut chesthe geometric ga unequal slices chesthav. Nene divide chestha.

Varun places the samosa back on the paper. He carefully positions his hands on either side, preparing to split it cleanly down the middle with both thumbs.

VARUN
Exactly fifty-fifty. No chutney bias. Clear?

ANANYA
Sare, jaldi kaani. Bus timing aypothundi.

Varun applies pressure. 

*CRUNCH.* 

The dry, crispy crust completely shatters. The entire potato filling bursts sideways, smearing across the newspaper, leaving one tiny hollow piece of crust in Varun's right hand and a messy pile of loose aloo on the paper.

Silence.

Varun stares at the shell in his hand. Then at the smashed filling on the paper.

ANANYA
(staring at the paper)
Great job, architect. Chala neat ga divide chesav.

VARUN
(clearing his throat, completely unbothered)
Idi... structural flaw. Samosa fried too hard. Dry coating.

ANANYA
Nee mechanics sariga levu ani opuko first-u.

Varun looks at the tiny piece of empty crust in his fingers. He silently holds it out toward her.

VARUN
Indha. Crust neeke isthunna. Outer layer crispy ga untadhi kada... neeku adhe istam.

Ananya looks at the tiny piece of baked dough, then up at Varun’s earnest, deadpan face.

ANANYA
Em matladuthunnav ra? Filling antha kindha padesi naku pottu isthunnava?

VARUN
Filling lekapothe carbs thakkuva Ananya! Health consciousness! Nenu nee betterment kosam sacrifices chesthunna.

Ananya shakes her head, a smile breaking through her annoyance. She reaches out, takes the tiny crust piece from his fingers, and picks up a small chunk of the potato filling from the paper with her other hand.

ANANYA
Nee daggara nunchi direct ga oppukovadam eppatiki kaadhu.

She pops the crust into her mouth, chewing slowly, staring at him.

VARUN
(watching her)
Taste ela undi?

ANANYA
Challabadi poyindi. Waste.

VARUN
Aithe migilindi nene thinta.

Varun instantly scoops up the rest of the loose aloo filling with his fingers and eats it before she can respond.

ANANYA
Rey! Motham thinesav!

VARUN
(talking while chewing)
Nuvve ga waste annav! Resource optimization!

Ananya just looks at him, fighting back a grin, and slaps his shoulder lightly with her notebook.

ANANYA
Pani ki rani logic lu matram baaga vasthay neeku. Naduvu, class ki time ayindi.

She stands up, pulling her bag strap onto her shoulder. Varun wipes his dusty fingers on a tissue, grinning quietly to himself as he gets up to follow her.
beat_summary: Varun and Ananya sit on a campus bench, arguing over who deserves the last remaining samosa based on who ordered vs. paid and their previous meal choices.
Ananya sarcastically yields the samosa to Varun, but Varun refuses to eat it, accusing her tone and eye contact of placing a guilt curse on him.
Varun attempts to split the samosa evenly down the middle with his hands, but the crispy crust shatters and spills the potato filling across the newspaper.
Varun hands Ananya the hollow crust piece with a absurd justification about health consciousness, which she reluctantly eats while mocking him.
Varun scoops up the remaining loose filling and eats it before Ananya can take more, and she lightly swats him with her notebook as they walk to class together.
